newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan will deal with excessive yen movements -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan will deal with excessive yen movements -- MOF.

text.p: Japan maintains its stance that it will deal appropriately with excessive movements of the yen's exchange rate, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.

"Excessive movements are never positive for continued growth without inflation. Our basic stance is that we will deal with them as approporiate every time. We will continue to keep close watch," he said.
Mitsuzuka said the Group of Seven (G7) nations held serious discussions on currency markets at their meeting in Washington in late April, with a common understanding and in a spirit of cooperation.
"I think it (the G7 statement on foreign exchange rates) is getting through (to the markets)," he said.

Asked whether the yen's strengthening had been too rapid, Mitsuzuka said Japan would deal with excessive strengthening or weakening of the yen in a timely and appropriate way. He added that he would take into account comments made on currency rates by business leaders such as the one made by the head of Keidanren on Monday.
"You should not look at the market in a short time span. You must look at it a little bit more," Mitsuzuka said.

Asked whether he was satisfied with the yen's strengthening against the dollar, he said: "It feels like it's about time. But I don't want to say whether the move has been sufficient or that I am satisfied with it."
Asked whether Japan's current low interest rates would contribute to continued growth without inflation, Mitsuzuka said: "It's as the Bank of Japan governor has been saying. I support that."
BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita has said Japan's current monetary policy aims to put emphasis on ensuring the basis for economic recovery.

Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of Keidanren, or the Federation of Economic Organisations, said on Monday that Japanese interest rates should not remain at their present low levels, which had plunged depositors into difficulties. He also said any steep currency fluctuation was undesirable and the yen's appropriate range was between 110 and 120 yen to the dollar.
